Alex B.: Heads up — I'm stepping out at 16:30 PST. Primary handoff for the overnight window is up for grabs; I have a calendar conflict. Anyone able to take primary?
Maria L.: I can take primary starting 16:30 until 00:30. Samir, can you be secondary?
Samir K.: Yep I can be secondary until 22:00. After that I'm out.
Alex B.: Awesome — Maria primary, Samir secondary until 22:00. We still need a secondary from 22:00 to 00:30.
Priya S.: I can cover 22:00–00:30 as secondary. I'll make sure the runbooks are pinned.
Alex B.: Thanks Priya. Quick note: we just got a low-volume surge on the embeddings host in us-west1. No pager yet but latency spiked ~2x for ~15m. I want us to be ready in case it escalates.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED — embeddings-us-west1 high p99 latency. Severity: informational. Link: https://monitoring/redwood/incident/9876
Maria L.: link reviewed. p99 at 1.2s, baseline 0.6s. Errors are not increasing, just latency. Sounds like transient batch backlog.
Samir K.: Agree. First action is confirm batching queue size and tail latencies. If queue > 50 and p99>1s, we page infra.
Priya S.: Quick runbook pointer: /runbooks/embeddings/p99-latency -> steps 1–4. Step 2 is to check batch size and heap pressure; step 4 triggers paging infra oncall.
Jamie T.: Adding: if errors > 0.5% OR 2+ customers report degraded throughput, escalate to SEV2 and page Platform oncall.
Maria L.: I'll watch for customer reports and error rate. Samir — can you run the quick checks (queue depth, GPU util, mem)?
Samir K.: Running now. cpu: 62%, gpu util: 84%, queue depth: 28, kv-cache hit: 72%. Nothing catastrophic. Allocated batchworker threads are at 12 of 16.
Alex B.: Good context. No page right now. Let's document the escalation threshold in this thread so whoever picks up knows what to do.
Maria L.: Escalation rules (summary):
- Page infra oncall if p99 >= 1.5s for >5 minutes OR queue depth >= 75 OR errors >= 0.5%.
- Page SRE lead (Jamie) if we see sustained customer impact or cross-region degradation.
- During handoff gaps, primary must handoff open incidents + state in 5 min; if no primary, escalate to oncall manager.
Samir K.: I'll post a short ci-check command here: `curl -s https://metrics/api?q=p99%20embeddings%20us-west1 | jq .value` — that'll return the p99.
Priya S.: Also: if the page fires, include these fields in the page: region, p99, queue_depth, error_rate, affected_models, recent deployment id. That speeds triage.
oncall-bot: PAGE SENT to infra-oncall (pager duty) — Incident 9876 — embeddings-us-west1 latency spike. Priority: PAGER.
Maria L.: I got the page. Escalation matrix: I'll own triage, Samir you're secondary. If infra needs assist after 15m, we call Jamie.
Samir K.: On it. I'll drop a short check into #incidents if I see error rate start climbing.
Alex B.: For handoff docs — Maria, can you add a 1-paragraph summary to the shift notes channel and link the runbook + recent metric query you ran? That helps the next primary.
Maria L.: Will do now. Creating note: "16:30 handoff: embeddings us-west1 p99 spike observed (1.2s -> 1.0s), queue depth 28, no error increase. Primary: Maria L. Secondary: Samir K. Backup: Priya S. Escalation: infra-oncall -> Jamie T. Runbook: /runbooks/embeddings/p99-latency. Cmd: curl ..."
Priya S.: One more operational tip: if infra suggests temporary throttling, enable prefix caching `kv_cache = true` in the staging config for a 30m window per runbook guidelines.
Jamie T.: Copy. I'll be reachable if we need to promote to SEV2. If anything looks like customer-facing degradation, page me immediately and mark the incident SEV2 in the incident tracker.
Maria L.: Noted. Ok handing over — I'm primary now. Alex, have a good off-shift.
Alex B.: Thanks all. Leaving this thread pinned to the shift notes.
Maria L.: (pin added)
